claims.claim: The mission has direct contributor value because it makes the documented first-run UI path reproducible from the public npm lockfile while keeping generated artifacts and Signoff control state out of product receipts.
claims.evidence: The sealed goal requires public npm lockfile reproducibility, ignored generated outputs, and Signoff patch receipts excluding control artifacts; AC-001 requires npm ci, UI typecheck/build, Python checks, clean generated-output status, and PATCH.diff inspection for .signoff paths.
claims.falsifier: If the current repository already supports a clean public npm ci, typecheck, production build, ignored generated outputs, and .signoff-free PATCH.diff receipts, the mission would add no value.

claims.claim: The slice appears feasible as a bounded metadata and receipt-filtering change without UI behavior changes, Python runtime dependencies, package-manager changes, install-flow changes, services, or protocol semantic changes.
claims.evidence: The charter constrains the work to lockfile normalization, generated-output ignore hygiene, existing control-path filtering, and a regression test, while explicitly excluding dependency upgrades, version changes, new package managers, services, and quorum/protocol changes.
claims.falsifier: If public npm install remains blocked after lockfile normalization by external registry/network constraints, or if receipt correctness requires protocol semantic changes rather than consistent filtering of existing control paths, the mission should stop or pivot.

claims.claim: The evidence standard is sufficient because it proves both the contributor install/build path and the failure-prone receipt/status boundaries directly.
claims.evidence: The required proof includes npm ci, npm run typecheck, npm run build:web, python3 scripts/test.py, python3 scripts/check_repo.py, generated dependency/build/cache status evidence, and a conformance test inspecting sealed PATCH.diff for .signoff paths.
claims.falsifier: If verification omits git status evidence for generated outputs or only checks command success without inspecting PATCH.diff contents for .signoff paths, proof is incomplete.

claims.claim: The proposed work is minimal if limited to public lockfile reproducibility, ignore rules for generated dependency/build/cache outputs, receipt path filtering, and a focused regression test.
claims.evidence: The sealed charter and spec forbid UI redesign, new package managers, services, Docker, databases, auth, cloud changes, runtime deps, dependency upgrades, version changes, broad cleanup, quorum changes, and weakened gates.
claims.falsifier: If implementation changes UI behavior, adds alternate install paths, commits generated outputs, changes versions or dependencies unnecessarily, weakens gates, or rewrites protocol/quorum semantics, it exceeds the mission scope.

advisors.cut: Cut UI redesign, new package managers, services, Docker, databases, auth/cloud work, Python runtime dependencies, dependency upgrades, version changes, broad cleanup, quorum changes, protocol semantic rewrites, weakened gates, private registry requirements, and committed generated outputs.
advisors.first_move: From a clean product baseline, run npm ci, npm run typecheck, npm run build:web, python3 scripts/test.py, and python3 scripts/check_repo.py, then inspect git status for generated dependency/build/cache noise and inspect sealed PATCH.diff for .signoff paths.
advisors.null_hypothesis: Do not proceed if the current clean baseline already passes public npm ci, UI typecheck/build, Python checks, generated-output cleanliness, and .signoff-free PATCH.diff receipt inspection, or if the only blocker is external/private registry access outside repository metadata.

claims.claim: The mission has clear contributor value because it makes the public first-run UI path reproducible and prevents Signoff receipts from exposing control artifacts instead of only the authorized product patch.
claims.evidence: The sealed goal and AC-001 require public npm ci, UI typecheck, UI production build, ignored generated dependency/build/cache outputs, and sealed PATCH.diff receipts with no .signoff paths.
claims.falsifier: If a clean checkout already passes npm ci, typecheck, build, Python checks, generated-output status cleanliness, and PATCH.diff excludes .signoff, then the mission has no remaining product value.

claims.claim: The mission is feasible as a bounded metadata, ignore, and filtering fix without changing runtime behavior or protocol semantics.
claims.evidence: The charter constrains the work to preserving one-path install, zero Python runtime deps, no UI/package-manager/install-flow/protocol/service/quorum changes, and allows metadata plus consistent control-path filtering and regression tests.
claims.falsifier: If public npm ci remains blocked by external registry/network after lockfile normalization, or PATCH.diff correctness requires a protocol semantic change, the mission must stop or pivot.

claims.claim: The proof standard is sufficient because it combines install/build commands, Python checks, generated-output status evidence, and a conformance test that directly inspects sealed PATCH.diff contents.
claims.evidence: The sealed evidence standard names npm ci, npm run typecheck, npm run build:web, python3 scripts/test.py, python3 scripts/check_repo.py, generated-output status evidence, and conformance verification that PATCH.diff excludes .signoff.
claims.falsifier: If verification omits clean generated-output git status or only tests receipt generation without inspecting sealed PATCH.diff for .signoff paths, proof is insufficient.

claims.claim: The minimal scope is exactly lockfile public-registry normalization, generated-output ignore coverage, receipt path filtering, and one regression test.
claims.evidence: The charter non-goals exclude UI redesign, new package managers, services, Docker, database, auth, cloud/runtime deps, dependency upgrades/version changes, broad cleanup, and quorum changes.
claims.falsifier: If the patch changes UI behavior, install protocol, package manager, service boundaries, dependency versions, quorum behavior, or commits generated outputs, it exceeds scope.

advisors.cut: Cut generated committed build artifacts, private-registry workarounds, compatibility shims, broad cleanup, and unrelated UI or protocol edits.
advisors.first_move: Implement the smallest diff that normalizes the lockfile, updates ignore rules, and filters .signoff from sealed receipt patches.
advisors.null_hypothesis: Do not sign off on claims based only on code inspection; require command output plus direct PATCH.diff inspection evidence.

decision.first_slice: Normalize lockfile registry URLs, ignore generated dependency/build/cache outputs, make receipt patch generation apply existing control-path filtering, and add the focused conformance test.
decision.rationale: Both independent advisors support proceeding and identify the same minimal route. There is no material conflict to cross-examine; the locked proof must come from commands and direct sealed PATCH.diff inspection.
